acceptance_items.description: SmartPLS documents graphical common-factor CB-SEM with maximum-likelihood estimation, configurable iterations and starts, two stopping criteria, three special-assumption switches, and three mean-structure choices.
acceptance_criteria: The settings contract exposes ML maximum iterations, configured starts, the documented default and one-zero strategies, gradient and objective stopping tolerances, each documented special assumption, and each documented mean-structure policy.
Every chosen option is stored in the recipe and Run Details and reaches the compiled parameter table; no dormant option is advertised.
A dated desktop capture inventories any additional current setting, option dependency, and disabled state not enumerated by the public page.

acceptance_items.description: The documented defaults are 1,000 maximum iterations, a 1e-6 gradient criterion, a 1e-9 function-value criterion, and no mean structure; starting-value tables define parameter-family values for the default and one-zero strategies.
acceptance_criteria: A new CB-SEM recipe records 1000, 1e-6, 1e-9, and no mean structure unless the user changes them.

The default strategy initializes loadings at 1.0, paths and covariances at 0.0, residual variances at 0.5 times indicator variance, and latent variances at 0.05; one-zero uses 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, and 1.0 respectively.
A live-app fixture records the initial UI state of each special-assumption switch instead of inferring it from its description.

acceptance_items.description: The documented estimand is a graphical covariance-based SEM whose constructs are common factors and whose covariance and optional mean structures are explicitly identified.
acceptance_criteria: Common-factor measurement, structural regressions, explicitly drawn covariances, configured starts, and mean/intercept constraints compile into executable parameters rather than presentation objects.

Special assumptions can add exogenous latent correlations, within-construct causal-indicator correlations, and fixed causal-indicator variances exactly as selected and disclose every implied parameter.

A dated model-shape inventory records the current desktop behavior for observed structural variables, cross-loadings, residual covariances, fixed/equality constraints, and reciprocal paths before those shapes are claimed.

acceptance_items.description: CB-SEM tests the hypothesized common-factor model against the covariance matrix of the observed data; a mean structure additionally consumes observed means.
acceptance_criteria: The result records the exact covariance matrix, sample size, variable ordering, and, when used, mean vector derived from or supplied with the analytical data.
Raw-data, covariance-matrix, and correlation-matrix routes are independently tested and only routes confirmed by a dated desktop fixture count toward behavioral parity.
Missing-value treatment, weights, and matrix metadata are never inferred or silently converted.

acceptance_items.description: The documented preparation constructs the observed covariance structure, optionally adds a mean structure, then applies selected parameter starts and special assumptions before ML optimization.
acceptance_criteria: Parameter-table compilation is deterministic under graph-ID and declaration reordering and records each free, fixed, derived, implied, and equality-constrained parameter.
Configured starting values override strategy values only when the documented switch is enabled; causal-indicator variance implication overrides a user value only when selected and is disclosed.
Scale handling and missing-data preprocessing are frozen by a separate data contract and cannot vary between GUI and CLI.

acceptance_items.description: The public page demonstrates CB-SEM results and textbook replication but does not enumerate every current table, statistic, precision rule, or report tier.
acceptance_criteria: A dated desktop capture enumerates every estimate, fit, residual, quality, convergence, parameter, and model-summary table with ordering, labels, precision, exclusions, and important-versus-complete behavior.
QuickPLS reproduces the frozen semantic inventory from one canonical result document across GUI, CLI, archive, CSV, XLSX, HTML, SVG, and PNG where applicable.
The current registry state remains partial and Labs despite release-qualified bounded evidence; this capture alone cannot promote the cell to full.

acceptance_items.description: The public documentation includes a result screenshot but does not define a complete analytical-chart contract.
acceptance_criteria: A dated current-desktop fixture inventories every chart, source table, selectable parameter, display default, accessibility label, and export behavior; an empty inventory must be evidenced.
Every implemented chart is a view over canonical stored values and cannot recompute or alter the fitted model.

acceptance_items.description: The documented optimizer must reach its gradient or objective stopping rule; mean structures require identification constraints, and downstream comparison requires identified, converged, admissible solutions.
acceptance_criteria: Underidentification, non-positive-definite input or implied covariance, singular information, nonconvergence, Heywood estimates, unstable feedback, and violated bounds produce specific diagnostics without fabricated standard errors or silent fallback.
The run records final objective, gradient norm, iteration count, termination reason, admissibility checks, and affected parameter IDs.
Changing a scientific diagram relation changes the compiled table and result or fails before execution with a corrective diagnostic.

acceptance_items.description: The documented workflow builds the CB-SEM model graphically, chooses ML algorithm settings, estimates the model, and inspects a linked result; textbook examples serve as behavioral fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: Diagram, parameter table, recipe, estimator plan, result, save/reopen, and exports preserve the same model semantics and exact run identity.
At least one successful and one invalid textbook CFA/SEM workflow pass through the packaged GUI and CLI with no network dependency.
Current QuickPLS coverage remains partial and the capability remains Labs until every documented and live-captured option cell is implemented and release-qualified.

acceptance_items.description: SmartPLS documents the number of same-size case-resample subsamples, most-important or complete output, percentile, studentized, or BCa intervals, one- or two-sided tests, significance level, and random or fixed seed.
acceptance_criteria: The recipe persists the requested resample count, result amount, interval method, test side, significance level, and seed policy/value.
Only interval and test combinations implemented for every selected parameter family are selectable; unsupported combinations fail in preflight.
A dated desktop capture records the exact current selectable resample values, parameter-family selectors, seed defaults, and control dependencies not stated by the page.

acceptance_items.description: The documented interval default is percentile and the documented significance default is 5%; 500 is suggested for an initial evaluation and 5,000 or 10,000 for final results rather than stated as a universal subsample default.
acceptance_criteria: A new recipe defaults to percentile intervals and alpha 0.05 and records those values explicitly.
The UI distinguishes a 500-replicate initial workflow from 5000/10000 final workflows without relabeling a recommendation as a fixed algorithm default.
Test side, result amount, seed policy, and any default replicate count remain open until verified by a dated current-desktop capture.

acceptance_items.description: The procedure follows an estimated CB-SEM model and applies inference to CB-SEM results such as structural path coefficients.
acceptance_criteria: Every selected bootstrap replicate refits the complete linked CB-SEM parameter table rather than perturbing only the requested output coefficient.
Fixed, equality-constrained, mean-structure, covariance, group, and moderation parameters are either correctly resampled and reported or rejected before execution with an option-specific reason.
A live result inventory identifies every parameter family covered by most-important and complete modes.

acceptance_items.description: Each bootstrap sample is drawn with replacement from the original dataset and contains the same number of observations as that dataset.
acceptance_criteria: The resample ledger stores or deterministically reproduces exactly n source-row indices for each requested replicate, with replacement, from the linked analytical sample.

Matrix-only input without case-level observations cannot be presented as case-resample bootstrap and returns a typed incompatibility unless an independently documented matrix-bootstrap contract exists.
Missing-data preprocessing occurs at the documented stage and is identical under fixed seed across GUI, CLI, and worker counts.

acceptance_items.description: Bootstrapping forms an empirical sampling distribution by same-n sampling with replacement and uses it to compute standard errors, p values, and selected nonparametric intervals.
acceptance_criteria: Percentile, studentized, and BCa computations use independently audited formulas and the same retained replicate ledger; studentization and BCa prerequisites are explicit.
Sign and factor orientation are aligned by a deterministic documented rule before summarizing latent-parameter distributions.
Failed or inadmissible fits remain counted with replicate index and reason and are never silently retried or replaced.

acceptance_items.description: The documented inferential outputs include empirical standard errors, confidence intervals, and p values, with a faster most-important set and a slower complete set.
acceptance_criteria: Every included parameter table links original estimate, bootstrap mean/bias where applicable, standard error, interval bounds, p value, test side, alpha, requested count, successful count, and failed-fit count.
A dated desktop capture freezes the exact most-important and complete table inventories, ordering, labels, precision, and significance presentation.
Current QuickPLS coverage and evidence remain absent and the cell remains Labs until full native, archive, packaged, oracle, and simulation qualification passes.

acceptance_items.description: The public page does not enumerate the current bootstrap charts or their display controls.
acceptance_criteria: A dated desktop capture inventories every distribution or interval chart, source replicates, selected parameter, reference line, defaults, accessibility semantics, and export behavior; an empty inventory must be evidenced.
Chart values round-trip from the canonical replicate/result payload and match the corresponding table summaries.

acceptance_items.description: Bootstrapping is downstream of CB-SEM estimation and becomes unreliable when the base model or too many resampled fits are unidentified, nonconverged, or inadmissible.
acceptance_criteria: An unidentified, nonconverged, or inadmissible base result blocks execution with exact corrective diagnostics.
Every failed replicate is retained; each table reports effective counts and suppresses inference with a typed reason when its pre-registered reliability threshold is not met.
Cancellation reaches a terminal cancelled state without committing a partial visible result or changing the archive.

acceptance_items.description: The documented workflow estimates CB-SEM first, uses about 500 subsamples for an initial evaluation, then 5,000 or 10,000 for final results and selects the appropriate result depth and inference options.
acceptance_criteria: The user can launch a bootstrap only from a compatible completed CB-SEM run, see workload/progress, cancel safely, and reopen/export the exact linked result.
Fixed-seed reruns reproduce resample indices and scientific results across supported worker counts; random-seed runs record the realized seed.
The UI explains the time tradeoff of replicate count and result amount without presenting an initial 500-replicate run as automatically final.

acceptance_items.description: The LRT setup selects a comparison model and applies matched estimator/optimizer settings, special assumptions, and one of the documented mean-structure policies.
acceptance_criteria: The setup selects an immutable compatible saved comparison run/model and displays the focal and comparison identities before execution.
Estimator, optimizer, special-assumption, and mean-structure differences are either normalized by an explicit documented workflow or blocked with the exact mismatch.
A dated desktop capture freezes all model selectors, option dependencies, and defaults not enumerated by the page.

acceptance_items.description: No mean structure is the documented default; the comparison contract requires the same estimation method and optimizer settings for both models.
acceptance_criteria: A new comparison uses no mean structure unless the linked runs use the same explicitly selected alternative.
The system does not silently re-estimate two saved results under hidden shared settings; any required re-estimation creates separately identified runs.
The initial state of each special-assumption switch remains open until a dated current-desktop capture verifies it.

acceptance_items.description: The documented LRT compares nested CB-SEM models in which the less restricted model has more free parameters and fewer degrees of freedom than the more restricted model.
acceptance_criteria: Nesting is validated from canonical parameter tables, equality labels, fixed values, and mean-structure constraints rather than filename or free-parameter count alone.
Adding or removing equality restrictions, fixed parameters, loadings, paths, or covariances is accepted only when it creates a mathematically nested pair over identical observed variables.
Non-nested theory alternatives are not labeled as this LRT.

acceptance_items.description: Both models must use the identical dataset and indicator set and therefore the same covariance matrix input.
acceptance_criteria: Dataset fingerprint, analytical row set, indicator identities/order, covariance matrix, sample size, missing-data treatment, weights, and mean vector where applicable must match exactly.
Same column labels over different data or differently filtered samples fail compatibility before calculation.
The report exposes each compatibility check and its source run.

acceptance_items.description: The LRT computes the more-restricted model chi-square minus the less-restricted model chi-square and evaluates it with the corresponding degrees-of-freedom difference.
acceptance_criteria: The focal and comparison orientation is derived from verified restriction nesting, and delta chi-square and delta degrees of freedom use that same orientation.
Matched ML objective scaling and degrees of freedom are independently checked on hand cases and external references.
No robust or scaled correction is applied or advertised unless its corresponding estimator and correction contract are separately implemented and qualified.

acceptance_items.description: The documented result is a chi-square difference test of equal fit versus better fit for the less restricted model, with degrees of freedom equal to the parameter-count difference.
acceptance_criteria: The result includes both run/model IDs, restriction orientation, each chi-square and df, delta chi-square, delta df, p value, decision threshold, and a semantic compatibility report.
A dated desktop capture freezes every additional table, label, precision rule, interpretation state, and export field.
Current QuickPLS coverage and evidence remain absent and the cell remains Labs until exact nesting, LRT, archive, and packaged qualification passes.

acceptance_items.description: The public page does not document an analytical chart for the LRT workflow.
acceptance_criteria: A dated current-desktop fixture confirms the chart inventory and its controls; an empty inventory must be evidenced rather than assumed.
Any QuickPLS comparison visualization is labeled as additional and derives only from the stored LRT payload.

acceptance_items.description: The documented LRT requires identical data and indicators, the same method/settings, identified and admissible converged solutions, and a nested model pair.
acceptance_criteria: Each failed prerequisite produces a distinct blocking code naming both affected runs and the exact mismatch or inadmissibility.
Negative delta df, inconsistent restriction mapping, ambiguous parameter correspondence, or non-nested models cannot yield a p value.
Historical or future-version runs that cannot prove semantic compatibility remain readable but comparison-ineligible.

acceptance_items.description: The documented user selects a comparison model file for a focal CB-SEM model, verifies the compatibility/nesting requirements, and interprets the chi-square difference test.
acceptance_criteria: The user can choose compatible immutable saved runs, see why incompatible choices are disabled, execute the LRT, and reopen/export the result with both source links intact.
Equality-constraint and omitted-parameter textbook fixtures cover significant and nonsignificant comparisons plus every documented invalid setup.
Model comparison used by invariance calls the same qualified LRT kernel and compatibility checks.

acceptance_items.description: SmartPLS MGA selects predefined groups and permits fixed-value, within-model equality, and across-group equality constraints while estimating the same SEM for each group.
acceptance_criteria: The setup persists an ordered group definition and every parameter constraint by stable parameter ID, value/equality label, and group scope.
Across-group constraints are distinct from equality constraints inside one group and compile into a simultaneous or mathematically equivalent group parameter table.
A dated desktop capture inventories group-count limits, selectors, estimator options, constraint editor behavior, and current defaults.

acceptance_items.description: Without user-specified cross-group constraints, SmartPLS estimates the same model separately for each selected group.
acceptance_criteria: New MGA setup imposes no across-group equality constraint unless the user selects one or enters an invariance workflow that defines it.
Identification constraints already present in the scientific model remain explicit and are not mistaken for substantive cross-group equality constraints.
Default group selection, reference group, estimator settings, and any comparison threshold remain open until current-desktop capture.

acceptance_items.description: The same CB-SEM structure is fitted across predefined subpopulations, with optional parameter constraints and established measurement invariance before substantive group comparison.
acceptance_criteria: Every group consumes the same canonical variables and relation topology, with differences expressed only through explicit group overrides and constraints.
Fixed loadings, equal loadings or paths, and across-group equality constraints affect the correct group parameter cells and survive save/reopen.
Arbitrary declared group counts are supported where the current SmartPLS fixture confirms them; pairwise-only behavior is never generalized to omnibus output.

acceptance_items.description: MGA uses predefined groups such as gender, region, or treatment and fits the common model to the observations in each group.
acceptance_criteria: The recipe records group-variable identity, allowed values/filters, stable labels, included and excluded counts, missing-group handling, and each group analytical sample fingerprint.
Groups are nonempty, disjoint when the selected workflow requires a partition, and evaluated against identical observed-variable bindings.
Case, frequency, and sampling weights are never treated as group membership and unsupported group-weight combinations fail preflight.

acceptance_items.description: SmartPLS estimates the specified model by group and applies fixed, equality, or across-group constraints selected by the researcher.
acceptance_criteria: Group sample statistics and likelihood contributions are computed from actual group rows; scaled-pooled or synthetic group estimates cannot satisfy the contract.
Parameter correspondence uses stable semantic IDs and remains invariant to group-label exchange after canonical relabeling.
Constraint compilation, identification, optimization, and admissibility diagnostics are retained separately for every group and for the combined constrained system.

acceptance_items.description: The documented purpose is to assess model stability and compare parameter estimates across subpopulations, subject to measurement invariance.
acceptance_criteria: Results include per-group sample counts, convergence/admissibility, estimates, standard errors and fit summaries, applied constraints, and valid cross-group parameter comparisons.
A dated desktop capture freezes every table, comparison statistic, reference-group convention, ordering, precision, chart, and export field.
Current QuickPLS coverage and evidence remain absent and the cell remains Labs until genuine group estimation, invariance linkage, and qualification are complete.

acceptance_items.description: The public MGA page does not enumerate group-comparison charts or their controls.
acceptance_criteria: A dated current-desktop fixture inventories every group chart, source table, group/parameter selector, default, accessibility semantic, and export behavior; an empty inventory must be evidenced.
Group colors always have non-color labels and chart values match canonical per-group tables.

acceptance_items.description: Measurement invariance is a documented requirement for meaningful MGA, and every selected group must support an identified, estimable common model.
acceptance_criteria: Missing or failed required invariance, empty groups, incompatible variables, underidentified group models, infeasible constraints, nonconvergence, or inadmissible group solutions block or qualify comparison with a typed group-specific reason.
Extreme imbalance and too-small groups receive workload/scientific diagnostics without silently merging or dropping a group.
No synthetic preview or pooled approximation is presented as MGA output.

acceptance_items.description: The documented workflow declares groups, establishes measurement invariance, estimates the same SEM per group with any selected constraints, and compares stable parameters.
acceptance_criteria: The setup links the exact invariance assessment, group definitions, constraints, model, data, and estimator recipe; stale dependencies invalidate rather than silently update the run.
Users can inspect group-specific and comparison results, save/reopen, and export with exact source links and constraint provenance.
Packaged fixtures cover two and multiple groups, constrained and unconstrained models, label exchange, imbalance, and invalid invariance.

acceptance_items.description: SmartPLS documents configural, weak/loading, strong/intercept, strong plus means, strict/residual, and strict plus means models, organized into basic and strict sequences.
acceptance_criteria: The setup exposes both complete predefined sequences and each documented model level with its exact loading, intercept, residual-variance, and construct-mean constraints.
Group selection and estimator/optimizer settings are stored with all generated nested models.
A dated desktop capture freezes sequence defaults, stopping behavior after a failed level, partial-invariance controls if present, and all disabled-state rules.

acceptance_items.description: The configural model is the documented unconstrained group default; the public page describes both basic and strict sequences but does not identify a universal default sequence.
acceptance_criteria: Configural estimation applies the same structure in every group with no across-group equality constraints.
QuickPLS does not invent a default basic-versus-strict sequence; the current desktop choice and any remembered preference require dated evidence.
Generated constraint sets are visible before execution and stored immutably.

acceptance_items.description: Invariance compares the same measurement structure across groups while progressively constraining loadings, intercepts, residual variances, and construct means.
acceptance_criteria: Configural uses the same structure; weak constrains all loadings; strong adds intercept equality and fixes construct means to zero only in the first group; strong-plus-means also equalizes construct means.
Strict adds residual-variance equality to strong while retaining first-group-zero/others-free means; strict-plus-means also equalizes construct means.
Identification constraints and substantive invariance constraints remain separately typed and auditable.

acceptance_items.description: The assessment uses predefined groups measured by the same indicator/construct structure so nested equality restrictions can be compared.
acceptance_criteria: The recipe records stable group definitions, per-group counts/fingerprints, shared indicator bindings, category/value coding where relevant, missing treatment, weights, and mean-vector availability.
Different indicator sets, transformations, analytical rows outside the declared grouping, or incompatible scale metadata block the sequence.
Every generated level uses the same frozen group samples and covariance/mean inputs.

acceptance_items.description: Basic proceeds configural, weak, strong, strong-plus-means; strict proceeds configural, weak, strong, strict, strict-plus-means and deliberately skips strong-plus-means.
acceptance_criteria: Generated parameter tables match the documented constraint additions at every level and preserve the exact sequence adjacency.
Each adjacent comparison uses the same qualified CB-SEM LRT kernel, data compatibility, nesting validation, and admissibility checks.
Group declaration order and label exchange leave aligned scientific conclusions invariant.

acceptance_items.description: The result must make each progressively constrained model and its nested comparison visible so users can judge whether measurement equivalence holds before MGA.
acceptance_criteria: For every level, results identify applied constraints, group estimates/fit/admissibility, chi-square and df, adjacent delta chi-square/df/p value, and the exact sequence decision.
A dated desktop capture freezes all tables, labels, decision wording, thresholds, precision, charts, and export fields.
Current QuickPLS coverage and evidence remain absent and the cell remains Labs until every predefined level and sequence is genuinely estimated and qualified.

acceptance_items.description: The public invariance page documents constraint tables and sequences but does not enumerate the current chart surface.
acceptance_criteria: A dated desktop fixture inventories every level/sequence visualization, source tables, selectors, defaults, accessibility semantics, and export behavior; an empty inventory must be evidenced.
Any QuickPLS progression visualization links every decision marker to its exact nested-test row and does not replace the table evidence.

acceptance_items.description: Meaningful invariance requires comparable group models whose progressively constrained forms remain identified, converged, admissible, and nested.
acceptance_criteria: Empty groups, mismatched structures, missing mean inputs, underidentification, infeasible equality constraints, nonconvergence, inadmissibility, or non-nesting stop the affected comparison with a level- and group-specific code.
A failed level is never silently skipped to claim a later level; downstream status names the unresolved prerequisite.
Partial invariance, if later supported, is explicitly user-authored and cannot overwrite the predefined complete-sequence result.

acceptance_items.description: The documented workflow evaluates a selected basic or strict nested-model sequence before substantive CB-SEM multigroup analysis.
acceptance_criteria: The user chooses groups and sequence, previews generated constraints, runs the levels with progress/cancellation, inspects each nested comparison, and links an accepted assessment to MGA.
Save/reopen and exports preserve every generated model, run identity, constraint set, comparison, warning, and decision without recalculation.
Packaged fixtures exercise every level, both sequences, pass/fail branches, group-label exchange, invalid inputs, and cancellation.

acceptance_items.description: SmartPLS currently documents two-way CB-SEM interactions with generic indicator, product indicator, mean centering, double mean centering, and orthogonalization approaches.
acceptance_criteria: The interaction dialog exposes exactly the documented computation approaches for an eligible two-way path and persists the selected approach with predictor, moderator, outcome, and moderated-path IDs.
Generated construct/indicator previews disclose the resulting number and binding of product indicators before execution.
A dated desktop capture freezes every approach-specific option, automatic main-effect rule, disabled state, and current default beyond the facts documented on the page.

acceptance_items.description: Double mean centering is the documented default interaction computation approach for SmartPLS CB-SEM moderation.
acceptance_criteria: A newly authored eligible interaction selects double mean centering unless the user chooses another documented approach.

Simple-slope display uses low, mean, and high moderator levels corresponding to one standard deviation below, the mean, and one standard deviation above; any alternate probe values require explicit selection.
Bootstrap settings retain their own documented defaults and are not silently inherited from point estimation.

acceptance_items.description: The user draws a moderation path from a moderator construct onto an existing predictor-to-outcome path, causing SmartPLS to generate a predictor-by-moderator construct linked to the outcome; only two-way interactions are supported.
acceptance_criteria: Moderation is stored as a scientific relation targeting a stable structural-path ID, and its generated interaction construct and outcome path compile into the CB-SEM parameter table.
Predictor, moderator, outcome, both main effects, interaction effect, and generated measurement terms survive save/reopen and remain traceable to the authored moderation relation.
Three-way and higher interactions are blocked as outside this parity contract instead of being routed through a PLS or LMS implementation.

acceptance_items.description: The documented approaches compute interaction indicators from the predictor and moderator indicators and estimate the generated interaction inside the linked CB-SEM model.
acceptance_criteria: Raw case-level indicator values and exact analytical rows are available for every product, centering, and orthogonalization operation.
Matrix-only input is rejected for approaches that require unobserved case-level products unless a separately documented sufficient-statistics implementation is qualified.
Missing handling, transformations, scales, and group filters are applied consistently to main-effect and generated interaction indicators and recorded in lineage.

acceptance_items.description: Product approaches multiply predictor and moderator indicators; mean centering centers before products; double mean centering additionally subtracts the product of indicator means; orthogonalization removes main-effect-explained product variance.
acceptance_criteria: Each approach is frozen with independently tested equations, indicator pairing/order, centering constants, residualization design matrix, and deterministic naming.

The generic and product-indicator approaches are distinguished by current-desktop fixtures wherever their generated terms or constraints differ; identical wording is not assumed to imply identical execution.
Generated columns are analysis-local derived terms with reproducible lineage and never overwrite source data.

acceptance_items.description: The documented workflow returns standardized path coefficients, uses CB-SEM bootstrapping for the interaction significance, and provides a simple-slope plot for interpretation.
acceptance_criteria: Results link the interaction estimate to its computation approach, main effects, conditional-effect equation, probe values, simple slopes, and bootstrap inference payload.
A dated desktop capture freezes the complete interaction, generated-indicator, conditional-effect, inference, fit, and interpretation table inventory with precision/export rules.
Current QuickPLS coverage and evidence remain absent and the cell remains Labs until product-indicator parity, bootstrap inference, probing, and packaged qualification pass.

acceptance_items.description: The documented Simple Slope Plot shows the predictor-to-outcome relationship when the moderator is one standard deviation below its mean, at its mean, and one standard deviation above its mean.
acceptance_criteria: The three labeled slope lines use stored conditional-effect coefficients and exact stored moderator mean/standard deviation; color is never the only differentiator.
A dated desktop capture freezes axis definitions/ranges, line defaults, confidence display if present, controls, table linkage, and image/vector export behavior.
Chart customization changes presentation only and never analytical probe values unless the user explicitly requests and reruns a new probe specification.

acceptance_items.description: The documented method requires an eligible existing structural path, predictor and moderator indicator sets, an estimable generated interaction, and a separate bootstrap run for significance.
acceptance_criteria: A missing/deleted target path, higher-order interaction, empty indicator block, zero-variance product, rank-deficient products, underidentified generated factor, nonconvergence, or inadmissibility returns an object-specific corrective diagnostic.
Product-count workload and collinearity are previewed before execution; no terms are silently dropped.
Point estimates without a successful linked bootstrap are never presented as bootstrap significance.

acceptance_items.description: The user defines predictor, outcome, and moderator constructs, draws the moderator onto the structural path, chooses an interaction computation, estimates CB-SEM, bootstraps the interaction, and inspects simple slopes.
acceptance_criteria: The complete authoring flow works by pointer and keyboard, displays generated terms before estimation, and keeps the scientific moderation relation synchronized with the parameter table.
Estimation, bootstrap, simple slopes, save/reopen, comparison, and exports maintain exact model/data/run linkage.
Packaged fixtures cover all five approaches, multiple eligible two-way interactions, invalid targets, high product counts, inference failure, and cancellation.

acceptance_items.description: SmartPLS CFA uses ML with maximum iterations, configured/default/one-zero starts, gradient and function-value stopping criteria, three special assumptions, and three mean-structure choices.
acceptance_criteria: CFA setup exposes and persists every documented ML optimizer, start, special-assumption, and mean-structure option while preventing structural-only settings from leaking into measurement-only analysis.
All settings compile into the same general CB-SEM parameter-table kernel with a CFA model-shape restriction rather than a separate numerical special case.
A dated desktop capture inventories any current CFA-only options, dependencies, and disabled states not present on the page.

acceptance_items.description: CFA documents 1,000 iterations, 1e-6 gradient and 1e-9 function-value criteria, no mean structure, Fabin-style default loading starts, and one-zero loading starts of 1.0.
acceptance_criteria: A new CFA recipe records 1000, 1e-6, 1e-9, and no mean structure unless changed; one-zero sets loadings/residual variances/latent variances to 1.0 and paths/covariances to 0.0.
The CFA page's Fabin-style default loading starts are implemented for CFA and not overwritten by the CB-SEM page's 1.0 default-loading table.
A dated same-version desktop fixture reconciles the page-specific difference and freezes exact Fabin computation and special-assumption switch defaults before full parity.

acceptance_items.description: CFA validates a hypothesized factor structure relating measured indicators to latent common-factor constructs before structural relationships are evaluated.
acceptance_criteria: Reflective common-factor loadings, factor covariances, indicator residual variances/covariances, cross-loadings, causal-indicator configurations where documented, fixed/equality constraints, and mean/intercept structures are represented in the canonical parameter table.
A measurement-only CFA cannot silently estimate structural regressions; selecting general SEM changes the declared analysis capability and recipe.
A dated desktop model-shape inventory confirms every authorable CFA relation and identification configuration before it is claimed.

acceptance_items.description: CFA models the covariance structure of measured indicators and optionally their means/intercepts under an identified mean structure.
acceptance_criteria: Results bind exact indicator ordering, sample size, covariance input, and, when used, mean vector to the linked dataset or supplied matrix metadata.
Raw, covariance, and correlation inputs are each advertised only after current-desktop behavior and scientific sufficiency are verified for the selected mean structure.
Scale, missing, group, weight, and transformation policies remain explicit and reproducible.

acceptance_items.description: The analytical input is converted to the covariance and optional mean structure, identification constraints are applied, and configured or selected default starts initialize ML optimization.
acceptance_criteria: Factor-scale identification, fixed/equality constraints, factor means, observed intercepts, residuals, and all implied special-assumption parameters compile deterministically by stable ID.
Fabin, one-zero, and configured starts are independently tested and recorded; no missing or invalid start is silently replaced during optimization.
The same preprocessed sufficient statistics and parameter table are consumed across GUI, CLI, archive revalidation, and oracle fixtures.

acceptance_items.description: The public CFA page demonstrates textbook-replicating results but does not enumerate every parameter, fit, residual, validity, diagnostic, or report table in the current desktop.
acceptance_criteria: A dated desktop capture freezes every measurement estimate, covariance/correlation, residual, fit, reliability/validity, modification, convergence, parameter, and model-summary table with exact ordering, labels, precision, and export behavior.
All outputs derive from the common canonical CB-SEM result model and identify CFA as measurement-only.
Current QuickPLS coverage remains partial and Labs despite release-qualified bounded ML evidence; capture alone cannot promote the cell to full.

acceptance_items.description: The public page includes a CFA result screenshot but does not define the complete analytical-chart surface.
acceptance_criteria: A dated current-desktop fixture inventories every CFA chart, source table, selector, default, accessibility semantic, and export behavior; an empty inventory must be evidenced.
Diagram result overlays and charts render stored canonical values and remain synchronized with parameter IDs after save/reopen.

acceptance_items.description: CFA optimization and optional mean structure require an identified factor model that converges to an admissible solution under the documented criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Underidentified factors/means, duplicate equality labels, non-positive-definite input, singular information, nonconvergence, Heywood estimates, invalid bounds, and inadmissible implied covariance produce typed object- and parameter-specific diagnostics.
No absolute-value variance conversion, zero-gradient substitution, or identity-information fallback can produce a successful result.
The result ledger records convergence/admissibility evidence even when inference or downstream comparison is blocked.

acceptance_items.description: The documented workflow graphically specifies a hypothesized factor model, estimates it with CB-SEM ML, and reviews the measurement results before structural modeling; textbook examples are available.
acceptance_criteria: Users can author by pointer and keyboard, inspect the synchronized parameter table, preflight identification/data, estimate, inspect results, and carry an accepted factor model into SEM without silent reinterpretation.
Textbook CFA fixtures cover covariance-only and mean structures, constraints, residual covariances, invalid models, save/reopen, and semantic exports in packaged and CLI flows.
Historical bounded runs remain readable and clearly distinct from newly compiled SemModelV4 runs.

acceptance_items.description: SmartPLS CB-SEM-project PCA offers standardized results only, based on the indicator correlation matrix, and uses eigenvalue decomposition.
acceptance_criteria: The parity settings do not offer unstandardized PCA results or a covariance-matrix computation mode.
The recipe records standardized/correlation/eigen decomposition and the retention rule even though each has only one documented parity value.
A dated desktop capture inventories any component-count override, missing-data setting, score option, rotation control, or disabled state before it is claimed.

acceptance_items.description: Standardized correlation-matrix outcomes are the only documented result type, and an eigenvalue of 1 is the decision criterion for retained components.
acceptance_criteria: A new PCA recipe explicitly records standardized correlation input and an eigenvalue-one retention threshold.

The boundary behavior at eigenvalue exactly 1, numerical tolerance, tie ordering, and any user override are frozen by hand cases plus a dated current-desktop fixture rather than inferred from the prose.
No rotation or inferential default is invented when the page does not document one.

acceptance_items.description: SmartPLS supports graphical PCA models that reduce observed indicators to uncorrelated principal components as exploratory analysis alongside, but not identical to, CB-SEM or PLS-SEM.
acceptance_criteria: PCA input variables and generated components have distinct observed/derived semantics and cannot be mislabeled as common factors or structural paths.
Graphical declarations, variable order, retained components, and presentation survive save/reopen and compile to the same PCA plan.
A dated desktop fixture freezes allowable graph shapes, minimum/maximum indicators, multiple PCA blocks, and any downstream score binding.

acceptance_items.description: The documented standardized PCA is based on the correlation matrix of the selected observed indicators.
acceptance_criteria: The result records selected indicator IDs/order, analytical row count, means and standard deviations used for standardization, correlation matrix, missing policy, and source fingerprint.
User-supplied correlation input is advertised only if a dated desktop fixture confirms it and required sample-size/metadata behavior is frozen.
Nominal, identifier, constant, nonfinite, and otherwise ineligible columns fail preflight with column-specific corrective guidance.

acceptance_items.description: The documented computation standardizes indicators, forms their correlation matrix, performs eigenvalue decomposition, and uses the eigenvalue-one rule to decide retained components.
acceptance_criteria: Standardization denominator, correlation convention, symmetric eigensolver, descending eigen ordering, sign orientation, near-tie handling, and retention-boundary tolerance are deterministic and independently tested.
Row and variable reordering preserve aligned results, and positive affine rescaling leaves standardized PCA invariant within the qualified tolerance.
Missing-data preprocessing and any score computation use the same stored standardization parameters.

acceptance_items.description: The public page describes uncorrelated components, captured variance, eigenvalues, and retention but does not enumerate every current results table or score/export option.
acceptance_criteria: A dated desktop capture freezes every eigenvalue, explained/cumulative variance, loading/vector, score, correlation, quality, retention, and summary table with ordering, labels, precision, and export rules.
Component sign alignment is documented so comparison and save/reopen do not report false scientific differences.

Current QuickPLS coverage remains partial and Labs despite release-qualified bounded PCA evidence; the shared cell cannot be promoted until both official PCA catalogue rows have their distinct workflows fully closed.

acceptance_items.description: The public page does not enumerate current scree, variance, loading, score, or biplot charts and controls.
acceptance_criteria: A dated current-desktop fixture inventories every PCA chart, source table, axis/component selector, retention marker, default, accessibility semantic, and export behavior; an empty inventory must be evidenced.
All chart points and thresholds round-trip from canonical result data and remain sign-aligned with tables.

acceptance_items.description: Standardized correlation-based eigen decomposition requires enough valid numeric indicators and rows, nonzero finite variances, and a usable symmetric correlation matrix.
acceptance_criteria: Too few indicators/cases, constant or nonfinite variables, missing-data exhaustion, malformed or non-symmetric correlations, materially non-positive-semidefinite input, eigensolver failure, and unrepresentable scores produce typed diagnostics.
Near-singular and repeated-eigenvalue cases use deterministic subspace/sign handling or clearly disclose non-unique orientation.
No NaN, infinity, silent variable deletion, or covariance-mode fallback reaches results.

acceptance_items.description: The documented workflow creates a graphical PCA model within a CB-SEM or PLS-SEM project, runs standardized eigen decomposition, and uses retained uncorrelated components for exploratory data reduction.
acceptance_criteria: Users can author/select indicators, preflight, estimate, inspect retention/results/charts, generate qualified scores where documented, save/reopen, and export with exact data/run provenance.
The CB-SEM-project catalogue entry and PLS-PCA entry share one scientifically identical kernel/evidence where applicable but preserve distinct official workflow references and acceptance rows.
Packaged fixtures cover micro exact, applied, repeated-eigenvalue, constant-variable, missing-data, save/reopen, export-readback, and keyboard workflows.
